correctness.rationale: The addition-chain relations force response coefficients inductively. A chain to p closes at the identity and yields py=0; a chain to p+1 either passes through p (truncate) or closes back at coefficient 1 and again yields py=0; a chain to p-1 closes after adding 1. In Z_q with q prime and q!=p this forces the first response to be the identity, contradicting the atomic identity relation. Yao's singleton bound then gives n+O(n/log n).

value.rationale: The result turns a factor-two prime-cyclic upper bound into n+O(n/log n), leaving only sublinear additive overhead above the known n+1 lower bound.
